content_of_post_to_comment: Fantasy authors will describe a 14-course royal banquet, but we all know the best-tasting meal in any fantasy novel is whatever stale rations are eaten on the side of the road after barely surviving an ambush.
comment: Maybe the real luxury in fantasy isn't abundance but contrast: after danger strips life down to survival, a simple meal becomes meaningful because the characters have finally earned the ability to taste it.
